from the uk capital gains tax (cgt) perspective, transfers of assets between spouses who are living together are generally exempt from uk cgt under “no gain, no loss” rule. -#tab#no cgt arises on the transfer regardless of market value of the asset at the date of transfer. -#tab#the transferee spouse (receiving) is treated as acquiring the asset at the transferor (giving) original base cost and original acquisition date, not at market value at transfer. -#tab#when the transferee spouse (receiving) eventually disposes of the asset to a third party, the chargeable gain is calculated using the original base cost at acquisition by transferor, not mv at transfer. the above assumes that both spouses are uk tax resident, hence in scope of uk cgt.
